findings.title: Hosted checkout confirm captures payment and posts a canonical ledger credit from an unverified, client-supplied provider_payment_id
findings.current_state: POST /v1/checkout/:cartId/confirm requires only that provider_payment_id be a non-empty 1-200 character string (services/api-gateway/src/routes/checkout.ts:638; schema packages/checkout-core/src/index.ts:116). It performs no provider signature verification, no assertProviderPaymentNotReplayed and no provider-side payment fetch, then calls PaymentExecutionAdapter.confirmPayment (checkout.ts:691 -> execution/payment-execution.adapter.ts:94) which invokes confirm_order_payment_with_ledger. That RPC sets orders.payment_status='paid', payment_transactions.status='captured', inserts payment_webhook_events with signature_valid=TRUE, and posts a balanced ledger transaction debiting pa_clearing and crediting merchant_payable (168_b1_b2_capture_refund_ledgering.sql:238). The route records whether the ledger row appeared (checkout.ts:713) into session metadata but never asserts on it.
findings.expected_state: Any transition of an order to paid, and any credit to merchant_payable, must be predicated on server-side cryptographically verified provider evidence and ideally a provider-side capture/amount confirmation — the standard the platform's own SaaS billing route already applies at routes/payments.ts:970-985 (status captured and amount >= expected).
assumptions: Reachability depends on the caller holding a valid signed handoff for a cart; that handoff is obtainable by the cart's own owner via GET /v1/storefront/:sub/cart/:token/checkout-url.

Whether the /v1/checkout router is exercised by any shipped client today is separate: the shipped storefront UI uses the storefront order-create route (ARCH-RESEARCH-003). The route is mounted and unauthenticated either way.
findings.risk: A shopper who legitimately obtains a signed handoff for their own cart can drive contact -> delivery -> payment-intent -> confirm with an arbitrary provider_payment_id string and receive a real, fully paid order with inventory committed and merchant_payable credited for money never received. That is free goods at unlimited scale plus a poisoned canonical ledger whose reconciliation compares against a compat table, not against provider settlement.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed: reject any non-COD hosted-checkout confirm that does not carry a provider signature verified server-side by the corresponding provider adapter, plus assertProviderPaymentNotReplayed, plus a provider-side capture/amount check via fetchRazorpayPayment. Until that lands, unmount /v1/checkout at services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:753.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting a signature or provider-fetch check between checkout.ts:638 and :691. Confirm with an integration test that posts a fabricated provider_payment_id and asserts the order does NOT reach payment_status='paid' and no ledger transaction is posted.

findings.title: ART-08's decisive change is unimplemented: the RLS + tenant-GUC backstop is DDL-real and runtime-dead, and every gateway query runs as service_role
findings.current_state: withTenantTx (services/api-gateway/src/lib/tenant-transaction.ts:15) is the only code that issues SET LOCAL ROLE app_tenant (:29) and the per-transaction GUC (:30). It is reachable only via withResolvedTenantTx (lib/tenant-context.ts:67), which has zero non-test callers repo-wide; the only other occurrence is a source-text assertion in __tests__/tenant-load-bearing-d4.test.ts:42. No runtime code anywhere sets app.site_id. Instead 114-116 non-test gateway files use getSupabaseAdmin (lib/supabase.ts:13-15), a SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY PostgREST client, wrapped only by a 124-line query-shape proxy (tenant/tenant-scoped.ts:52-77) that asserts a tenant COLUMN NAME appears in a predicate and never that its VALUE matches the session. The proxy intercepts only .from(), so all .rpc() calls bypass it; three sites construct a raw service client directly (middleware/auth.ts:133, routes/auth.ts:1342, routes/employee.ts:235). The DB backstop is absent for two independent reasons: migration 163 creates FOR ALL TO service_role USING(true) WITH CHECK(true) policies on orders (163:11), products (:27), sites (:92), subscriptions (:159), billing_history (:172) and super_admin_allowlist (:186) with no later DROP; and migration 196:29-35 states in its own header that postgres and service_role carry BYPASSRLS which overrides FORCE.
findings.expected_state: Constitution R-1/R-2 (LETBUYY_CONSTITUTION.md:392-393): no tenant query may run under a BYPASSRLS or blanket service_role connection; tenant data runs under the non-BYPASSRLS app_tenant pooled connection with SET LOCAL app.site_id derived from a validated token claim. ART-08 (:193-195) names this 'The decisive change'. DOC 05 P2 exit-gate blocks P3 and P8 until it closes.
evidence: rg -n withResolvedTenantTx over *.ts/*.mjs -> definition + one test assertion only (re-run by this author at 5af69e0c)
assumptions: TWO adversarial verifiers reached DIFFERENT severities on this same underlying fact, along a defensible axis, and BOTH are recorded rather than one being silently preferred. (a) The governance-drift verifier CONFIRMED it at S0 as an UNMET CONSTITUTIONAL OBLIGATION: ART-08's decisive change is entirely unwired, and DOC 01 calls this layer load-bearing. (b) The dedicated S0-C verifier corrected it to S1 as an EXPLOITABLE VULNERABILITY: it is a MISSING CONTROL, not a self-contained exploit - reaching cross-tenant data additionally requires a route-level defect, and two application-side compensating controls still stand.

RESOLUTION USED THROUGHOUT THIS PACKET: S0 as a governance/constitutional defect; S1 as an exploitability rating. 03_CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE_AS_BUILT.md B.8 and 05_DRIFT_AND_CONFLICT_REGISTER.md record the same split.

Two structural shapes supply the additional defect the exploit would need: tables absent from tenant-tables.registry.ts get no guard at all (tenant-scoped.ts:119), and 77 .rpc( call sites are never intercepted by the proxy (tenant-scoped.ts:115).

Migration 164_d4_tenant_role_guc.sql:20-22 grants app_tenant TO service_role, which carries BYPASSRLS and therefore overrides FORCE - so even a wired app_tenant path would need the grant chain re-examined.

The app_tenant mechanism may be architecturally unreachable from the current data layer: PostgREST/supabase-js cannot issue SET LOCAL ROLE. Choosing the connection strategy is a prerequisite, and is very likely WHY it was never wired.
findings.risk: The database-enforced tenant boundary is not load-bearing for any request. A single missed or wrong site_id predicate in any of ~1,300 query sites reads or writes another merchant's orders, customers, catalog or payments with full service_role authority and no DB-level deny. Migration 196 documents a real instance of exactly this class (site-private theme rows readable through a baseline USING(true)).
findings.recommendation: Route the highest-blast tenant tables (orders, store_customers, products, sites, payment_transactions) through withResolvedTenantTx on the pooled app_tenant connection, and add a validator that fails when a file imports getSupabaseAdmin and touches a tenant-tables.registry.ts table without a tenant-transaction boundary. Note the PostgREST blocker recorded in 07_CAPACITY_MODEL.md Finding C-6: supabase-js cannot issue SET LOCAL ROLE, which is very likely why app_tenant has no callers — the data-access layer change is a prerequisite, not a detail.
findings.trigger: Unconditional correctness fix. No measured signal required.
findings.verification: Falsify by producing a request path that executes SET LOCAL ROLE app_tenant against production traffic. Confirm by running the RT red-team suite against the full 000..197 replay with the gateway's actual client factory, and by SELECT polname, polroles::regrole[] FROM pg_policy on orders/sites in the live database.

findings.title: The production rate limiter is a non-atomic read-modify-write on Cloudflare KV, whose vendor-documented 1-write-per-second-per-key ceiling the code converts into an isolate-wide 60s-to-10min 503 outage of every /v1 data route
findings.current_state: services/api-gateway/wrangler.toml:259 sets RATE_LIMIT_KV_FALLBACK='on' for production, with a committed founder note dated 2026-08-01 stating Upstash Redis is the intended backend, that no UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN is provisioned, and that each limited request costs one KV write. Both KV paths are read-then-write with no atomic primitive or CAS: checkKvRateLimit (middleware/rateLimit.ts:320-325) and checkKvQueryCostLimit (:618-623). The query-cost limiter is mounted globally on /v1 (index.ts:684-688) with a narrow skip list (:356-371) and keys unauthenticated traffic by CF-Connecting-IP (:1029). On a KV error the module-level queryCostKvUnavailableUntil (:42, set at :627, 60s or 600s per :577-583) suppresses the limiter for EVERY key in that isolate and the middleware returns 503 RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE (:1078-1088) rather than 429. The fixed-window limiter auto-enables KV in production with no flag (:860, isProduction || flag). Production binds the shared CACHE namespace (wrangler.toml:313-316), not the letbuyy-rate-limit-production namespace declared at config/cloudflare/resource-names.json:63-66.
findings.expected_state: A rate-limit backend with atomic increment and no per-key write ceiling. The Upstash Redis path already implemented at rateLimit.ts:170-187 and :644-680 uses EVAL with INCR/SET and is genuinely atomic. Cloudflare's own documented remedy for this workload is a sharded Durable Object or the native Rate Limiting binding.
evidence: evidence/21-vendor-digest.md (Cloudflare KV: 1 write/second/key hard limit returning HTTP 429; 60s eventual consistency)
assumptions: Whether the KV path is the LIVE production backend depends on whether UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN are set on the production Worker. Repository evidence for their absence is the wrangler.toml comment and docs/runbooks/production-api-rate-limit-backend.md:81-82; the adversarial pass corrected that specific sub-claim to INFERRED, not VERIFIED. See ARCH-RESEARCH-076.
The vendor per-key write limit is taken from the primary-source vendor digest accessed 2026-08-16; it is not measured against this account.

Severity aligned to the adversarial verdict (S1). Capacity impact is nonetheless first-order: see 07_CAPACITY_MODEL.md Finding C-1. Vendor primary source: Cloudflare KV is 1 write/second/key HARD, returning HTTP 429.
findings.risk: Two independent failures. (1) Under concurrency the limiter under-counts — N simultaneous requests each read the same counter and each write value+1, so the counter advances by 1 instead of N, and KV's 60s cross-PoP consistency makes the effective limit per-PoP rather than global. That is a security defect, not only a capacity one. (2) The second concurrent request against the same key in the same second receives a vendor 429, which trips the isolate-global backoff and returns 503 on every non-exempt /v1 data route for 60 seconds, or 10 minutes on a quota-shaped error. This is a self-inflicted denial of service that triggers at roughly two concurrent requests sharing a key — orders of magnitude below the governed 10,000-merchant envelope. Server-side gateway calls from Vercel functions collapse onto a small egress-IP set and therefore onto very few keys.
findings.recommendation: Replace the backend. Preferred: a SHARDED Durable Object limiter keyed by idFromName (Cloudflare's documented pattern, ~1,000 rps soft ceiling per object) or Cloudflare's native Rate Limiting binding. Do NOT promote the existing single RUNTIME_COORDINATOR object into a global limiter — a singleton DO serialises everything addressed to it. Alternatively provision Upstash and remove RATE_LIMIT_KV_FALLBACK per the runbook's own exit criterion. Separately, stop server-side callers (apps/marketing-site/src/app/api/founding-pricing/route.ts:13-26) from sharing one rate-limit key.
findings.trigger: Already binding. Falsifiable now with a two-concurrent-request test against one key. Escalation signal: any 503 RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE in production logs.
findings.verification: Falsify by demonstrating an atomic KV increment primitive or by proving Redis is the live backend. Confirm by issuing 2 concurrent requests sharing a rate-limit key against a KV-backed deploy and observing a KV 429 followed by 503 on unrelated /v1 routes from the same isolate.

findings.title: The storefront's effective cache hit ratio on HTML and on gateway data fetches is approximately zero, from three independent and individually small causes
findings.current_state: Three layers that should absorb buyer traffic are all defeated. (1) Full Route Cache / ISR is unreachable: apps/storefront-runtime/src/app/store/[subdomain]/layout.tsx:76 unconditionally awaits resolveThemePreviewToken -> cookies() (src/lib/theme-preview-server.ts:12), forcing the whole /store/[subdomain]/** subtree to dynamic rendering; next.config.ts has no experimental block and Next 16.1.6 defaults cacheComponents:false, so every `export const revalidate` in that subtree is inert for HTML. (2) The Next Data Cache and per-render memoisation are defeated: src/lib/api/client.ts:45 sets a fresh X-Request-ID: crypto.randomUUID() on every server-side gateway fetch, and Next 16.1.6 hashes all init headers except traceparent/tracestate into both cache keys (incremental-cache/index.js:240-259; dedupe-fetch.js:60-82). All 19 storefrontReadInit(30-60s, tags) reads therefore write entries that can never be read again, and duplicate fetches within one render are not deduplicated. (3) The Worker Cache API tier (lib/storefront-cache.ts:107-130) has no request coalescing and no serve-stale path; stale-while-revalidate=300 is emitted as a header string only (:13, :24-26) and drives no background refresh. revalidateTag is called zero times repo-wide, so the declared tags are inert.
findings.expected_state: 06_10M_WORKLOAD_DEFINITION.md §6 established that reducing the uncacheable fraction is worth up to 8x, versus <=1.15x for cache-hit tuning. The governed model is 'SSR/ISR + Worker cache'. The base-case model assumed a 30% uncacheable share.
evidence: services/api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts:292 (gateway already synthesizes a request id when the header is absent)
assumptions: The ~100% uncacheable measurement is derived from source reading of the three mechanisms, not from a production hit-rate metric — no such metric exists (ARCH-RESEARCH-089).

Whether Vercel's edge honours the `public, max-age=300` header set at next.config.ts:124-126 on dynamic function responses is provider behaviour not testable from the repository; see ARCH-RESEARCH-097 for the security consequence if it is honoured.

Severity aligned to the adversarial verdicts on its three component findings (S2 each). Combined capacity impact is first-order: see 07_CAPACITY_MODEL.md Finding C-2. All three causes verified first-hand (evidence/06-storefront-cache-zero-hit-ratio.txt).
findings.risk: Every buyer page view executes a Vercel function, which calls the gateway, which queries PostgreSQL, which also writes telemetry rows. Modelled origin load is multiplied by roughly 3.3x at every band relative to the 30%-uncacheable base case. It also removes the CDN buffer in front of Vercel's 1,000-concurrent-per-10-seconds-per-region burst governor, so a flash sale is rejected with 503 FUNCTION_THROTTLED rather than absorbed.
findings.recommendation: Three small, independent, zero-infrastructure fixes, in this order: (a) drop the random X-Request-ID from the outbound fetch init (the gateway already synthesizes one, so traceability is unaffected); (b) move the theme-preview cookie read out of the tenant layout or behind a Suspense boundary so the public subtree can prerender; (c) add an in-isolate single-flight promise map around cachedJson. Then wire revalidateTag or the cache-version bump on catalog/navigation/page mutations (ARCH-RESEARCH-084) before raising any TTL. This is the single largest capacity lever in the packet and carries no constitutional risk.
findings.trigger: Already binding. Measurable once cache-state telemetry exists (ARCH-RESEARCH-089): hit ratio < 20% on storefront read paths.
findings.verification: Falsify by producing a `next build` output showing /store/[subdomain]/product/[productId] as static or ISR, or by measuring a non-zero Next Data Cache hit rate. Confirm by instrumenting X-Storefront-Cache and the Data Cache and reporting hit ratios per namespace.

findings.title: The live public order-create route bypasses the ART-14 signed cart handoff entirely and is unauthenticated, un-bot-gated, and commits inventory for COD with zero payment
findings.current_state: router.post('/:subdomain/orders', ...) is registered on the storefront router (services/api-gateway/src/routes/storefront/checkout-payment-routes.ts:251 via public-routes.ts:763) and mounted at index.ts:752, twenty-seven lines before api.use('/*', authMiddleware) at index.ts:779. It accepts a subdomain, customer details and item ids and creates a real order with committed inventory. There is no signed-handoff check, no customer-session requirement and no Turnstile (Turnstile is wired only for customer registration, storefront/customer-registration.ts:48). This is the path the shipped storefront UI uses (apps/storefront-runtime/.../checkout-client.tsx:414 -> app/api/orders/route.ts:48). For payment_method='cod' the order is created with status='confirmed' (166_d6_checkout_handoff_inventory.sql:199) and inventory committed (166:221) with payment_transactions.status='pending'. The only throttle is the global query-cost bucket (index.ts:684, 20 points/sec refill, capacity 200).
findings.expected_state: ART-14 / R-11 require the public order-create path to be reachable only behind the cart-bound signed handoff from the hosted checkout origin, with the server-authoritative cart as the source of the order lines.
assumptions: The signed-handoff machinery (cart digest, HMAC, expiry) is correctly implemented on the /v1/checkout path; the defect is that the live path does not use it.

Adversarially corrected S0->S1. Mount order confirmed (handler index.ts:752, authMiddleware index.ts:779, Hono composes in registration order). Throughput is bounded by a per-source-IP limit of 20 orders / 5 min, and target products need an inventory_levels row at an active location.
findings.risk: The entire ART-14 investment is inert on the live path. Anonymous callers can create unlimited COD orders that commit stock with zero payment, exhausting every SKU in a targeted store and flooding fulfilment queues. There is no cart binding, so the client posts item ids and quantities directly rather than the server cart being authoritative. An unauthenticated write endpoint that runs ~15 DB round-trips and a 30-40 statement locking transaction per call is also the cheapest way to saturate the database.
findings.recommendation: ARB must decide the V1 checkout topology: either make the hosted handoff the sole order-create entry and gate /storefront/:subdomain/orders behind it, or explicitly retire the hosted-checkout path and add a customer-session or Turnstile gate plus a per-(site, IP) order budget plus a server cart binding to the storefront route. Gate COD creation behind the existing risk engine before inventory is committed rather than after.
findings.trigger: Unconditional correctness fix; the abuse-rate ceiling is set by the adversary, not by the platform.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting a handoff/session/bot gate on the route before index.ts:779. Confirm by issuing an unauthenticated POST /v1/storefront/<sub>/orders with payment_method='cod' against a staging deploy and observing inventory_levels.available decrement.

findings.title: create_checkout_order rejects 'cashfree' although four routes and the payment adapters accept it
findings.current_state: Migration 170 DROPs the 14-argument create_checkout_order (170:27) — the exact overload migration 075's DO block had patched to allow cashfree (075:50-62) — and recreates a 16-argument version whose guard is IF p_payment_method NOT IN ('razorpay','stripe','paypal','cod') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION (170:81). Cashfree is gone. Meanwhile StorefrontCreateOrderBody.paymentMethod accepts 'cashfree' (checkout-payment-routes.ts:56), the hosted checkout accepts it (checkout.ts:144), and cashfree order/verify routes exist (checkout-payment-routes.ts:701 onward).
findings.expected_state: The set of payment methods accepted by the HTTP layer must equal the set accepted by the canonical order RPC, or the mismatch must be an explicit, tested rejection.
findings.risk: Any shopper selecting Cashfree gets a 500 from 'Order creation failed: unsupported payment method: cashfree' after passing validation. A silent regression introduced by a migration whose own header claims call-compatibility, covered by no test.
findings.recommendation: Either add 'cashfree' back to the guard in a new migration, or remove cashfree from StorefrontCreateOrderSchema, checkout.ts:144 and the cashfree routes. Add a contract test asserting the route-level payment-method enum is a subset of the RPC guard list.
findings.verification: Falsify by finding a later migration restoring cashfree. Confirm with a request selecting cashfree against staging.

findings.title: The live observability tables have no retention and are never pruned
findings.current_state: worker_request_logs (000_baseline.sql:13224), runtime_telemetry_metrics (:11603) and operation_metrics (:9939) are plain heap tables with no retention function, no prune job and no DELETE anywhere in database/, services/ or scripts/. Retention exists only as metadata plus detach_expired_hot_table_partitions() (079:265) acting on the *_partitioned SHADOW copies, driven solely by scripts/migration/run-hot-table-partition-maintenance.mjs:31-34 and .github/workflows/hot-table-partition-maintenance.yml; 079:1-2 states the live rename-swap is intentionally not performed. detach_expired_hot_table_partitions only DETACHes and marks partitions 'cleanup-required' (079:295-302) — nothing drops them, and docs/governance/hot-table-retention-governance.md confirms physical cleanup is a manual operations action. operation_metrics is excluded from the retention_policies_target_table_check allowlist (079:24) and can never receive a policy, as are runtime_telemetry_spans and runtime_structured_logs. Migration 131:110-141 additionally mirrors every live row into the shadow, so each row is physically written twice.
findings.expected_state: High-cardinality request-log and metric tables on the single PostgreSQL source of truth must have enforced retention.
assumptions: Time-to-exhaustion is INFERRED; no capacity model or disk-utilisation measurement exists in the repository.
worker_request_logs is sampled at 2% for anonymous storefront GET/HEAD only; runtime_telemetry_metrics is unsampled per request, so total row volume is undiminished.
findings.risk: Unbounded growth of the two highest-write tables plus their shadow mirrors on the same PostgreSQL instance as the canonical ledger: disk exhaustion, index bloat, autovacuum pressure and a steadily worsening p95 on every co-resident query. Supabase enters read-only mode at disk-full and clears only below 95% utilisation (21-vendor-digest.md), which would stop order writes.
findings.recommendation: Either complete the partitioned swap under ARB approval so the existing detach job applies to live data, or add a bounded retention job against the live tables. Do not ship to 1,000 merchants with the mirror trigger active and no pruning. Escape hatches exist today: manual DELETE, set_hot_table_partition_shadow_mirror_enabled(false) at 131:59, disk scaling.
findings.trigger: Disk utilisation above 70%, or worker_request_logs row count above a stated budget.
findings.verification: Falsify by finding any prune path against the three live tables. Confirm with SELECT pg_total_relation_size on each and a growth-rate measurement.

findings.title: Partition shadow-mirror triggers are ENABLED on five live hot tables, doubling every outbox and queue write; the Constitution requires the mirror disabled and it has already caused a total outbox outage
findings.current_state: 131_hot_table_partition_shadow_mirror.sql:112-141 creates five AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ... FOR EACH ROW triggers on the LIVE tables worker_request_logs, runtime_telemetry_metrics, outbox_events, platform_queue_jobs and webhook_deliveries, each executing mirror_hot_table_partition_shadow() (131:9-56), which per row SELECTs from retention_policies and runs a dynamic INSERT INTO <shadow> SELECT ($1).*. A kill switch set_hot_table_partition_shadow_mirror_enabled(boolean) exists at 131:58 with NO caller in any migration, script or workflow. Migration 179's header (:1-11) is direct evidence the mirror executes against live traffic: a missing shadow column raised SQLSTATE 42601 and 'broke EVERY outbox write — including theme release publishing via publish_theme_release()'. outbox_events is touched at least three times per event (INSERT by the RPC, UPDATE by claim, UPDATE by complete), so the trigger fires three times per event.
findings.expected_state: LETBUYY_CONSTITUTION.md:296 — 'the partition-shadow seam (kept, mirror disabled)'; :316 lists partitioning-now among rejected constructs with 'the partition helper seam exists, disabled'. DOC 04 LEG-057/LEG-068 order the mirror disabled.
assumptions: Whether the mirror is enabled in the production database is UNKNOWN from the repository; the trigger DDL is committed and no migration disables it, and migration 179's incident narrative is first-party evidence that it fired in a production-shaped environment.
findings.risk: Every write to the transactional outbox and the queue-job table is doubled and pays a per-row catalog lookup plus a dynamic-SQL EXECUTE inside the caller's transaction. Any column drift between a live table and its shadow aborts the live write — which has already happened once and broke all outbox writes, i.e. checkout side effects and theme publishing. This is an availability-critical coupling on the money path, and it buys nothing: the live tables remain unpartitioned heaps with no retention.
findings.recommendation: Ship a paired migration that drops the five mirror triggers (or calls set_hot_table_partition_shadow_mirror_enabled(false)) restoring the constitutionally required disabled-seam state, and add a validator asserting no mirror_hot_table_partition_shadow trigger is attached. If the mirror is genuinely wanted it needs a Constitution amendment plus a column-drift guard. Retarget migration-safety-validator.mjs accordingly (ARCH-RESEARCH-060).
findings.trigger: Unconditional; the Constitution forbids the current state.
findings.verification: Falsify by finding a later migration dropping or disabling the triggers. Confirm against the live database with SELECT tgname FROM pg_trigger WHERE tgfoid = 'mirror_hot_table_partition_shadow'::regproc.

findings.title: Inventory reserve and commit are collapsed into one transaction — stock is hard-decremented before payment and the TTL reservation lifecycle is never exercised by checkout
findings.current_state: create_order_with_inventory_reservations calls reserve_inventory with a 1200s TTL at 166_d6_checkout_handoff_inventory.sql:134 and then commit_inventory_reservation at 166:221 inside the SAME transaction, so inventory_levels.available is decremented at order-creation time for prepaid orders that are not yet paid. No checkout step creates a standalone reservation: checkout_sessions.inventory_reservation_ids (added at 146:18) is read at routes/checkout.ts:393 but written by zero code paths, so the confirm-time reservation revalidation at checkout.ts:394-403 is unreachable dead code. There is no extend/renew RPC.
findings.expected_state: ART-15: reserve-with-TTL at checkout entry, extend while the shopper is active, expire on abandonment, commit only on payment success, release on failure — one lifecycle, not a pre-payment hard decrement.
findings.risk: Every abandoned prepaid checkout permanently removes stock until an operator cancels the order — the sweeper cannot help because the reservation is already 'committed', not 'active'. Conversely a shopper who completes contact/delivery/payment-intent holds no reservation at all and can be told at confirm that the last unit is gone. Oversell and undersell are both reachable. Because reserve and commit share one transaction, the per-SKU inventory row lock is held for the entire 30-40 statement order transaction.
findings.recommendation: Split the lifecycle: reserve at hosted-checkout entry or at checkout-URL issuance, persist the reservation ids into checkout_sessions.inventory_reservation_ids, commit only inside the payment-confirmation transaction, and release on failure or expiry. Delete the dead revalidation branch or make it real.
findings.trigger: Unconditional correctness fix; abandoned-cart rate above ~50% makes the revenue impact immediate.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting a writer for checkout_sessions.inventory_reservation_ids. Confirm with a behavioural test: abandon a prepaid checkout and observe inventory_levels.available does not recover.

findings.title: No golden signal for PostgreSQL saturation is emitted anywhere in source
findings.current_state: Searching the repository for pg_stat_activity, pg_stat_database, pg_locks, pg_stat_statements and max_connections outside tools/ and prose returns only descriptive strings in LCIS tooling, which itself declares them NOT CONNECTED (packages/lcis-adapters/src/postgres/PostgresAdapter.ts:185-189). No runtime, cron, migration or health route reads connection count, active/idle counts, lock wait or slow-query statistics. The pooled client is configured at max 5 connections per isolate with connect_timeout 5s and no statement timeout (packages/infrastructure/pooled-sql-adapter/index.ts:51-56).

The JS side round-trips through IEEE754 Number and GST maths crosses the boundary twice (gateway computes minor, passes numeric to the RPC, RPC stores rupees, invoice re-derives minor). numeric(10,2) on payment_transactions also caps a single transaction at Rs 99,999,999.99. findings.title: Storefront Razorpay verification grants value on signature alone, with no provider-side capture or amount confirmation

Combined with ARCH-RESEARCH-018 (reconciliation not pushed) and the absence of saturation signals, every capacity ceiling in this packet becomes a silent outage.

findings.title: The push dispatcher runs dry-run in production and counts every dry run as sent

The result is written into the notification dispatch log by the consumer (platform-queue-consumer.ts:665-676). production-deploy.yml provisions no FCM/APNS secrets for queue-workers (it sets only INTERNAL_API_SECRET and QUEUE_TENANT_ENVELOPE_SECRET).

findings.risk: Production dashboards and the notification dispatch log report N pushes sent when zero devices were contacted. Nobody discovers push notifications are entirely non-functional until a merchant or customer complains, because every automated signal says success. This is the exact failure the mock-honesty rule exists to prevent. It also means any capacity or cost model built on today's telemetry records the per-message external-call cost of push as zero.

Assert in CI that no production var block sets a *_MODE to dry-run/mock while the corresponding secrets are placeholders, or make the adapter refuse to construct in a production ENVIRONMENT with placeholder credentials. Record push dispatch as an explicit Class-A skip in production-safety-preflight.json, or provision the credentials.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting a distinct dry-run status. Confirm by reading the dispatch log after a dry-run batch and observing sent > 0 with zero provider calls.

findings.title: The events backbone is a non-atomic post-commit outbox dual write at 38-40 TypeScript call sites
findings.current_state: EventExecutionAdapter.emitDomainEvent issues a standalone PostgREST .from('outbox_events').upsert() after the caller's RPC has already committed (services/api-gateway/src/execution/event-execution.adapter.ts:60-77), across 38 non-test call sites in 28 files. The storefront checkout path is confirmed post-commit (checkout-payment-routes.ts:411 runs after db.rpc('create_checkout_order') at order-execution.adapter.ts:158). No trigger writes outbox rows and no reconciliation sweeper exists, so loss is uncompensated. checkout.completed is emitted by BOTH paths with DIFFERENT idempotency keys — SQL 'checkout.completed:'||v_order_id versus TS `checkout.completed:${session.id}:${body.idempotency_key}` (checkout.ts:739) — producing duplicate outbox rows and double-firing consumers. tests/federation/event-spine-contracts.test.mjs:153-235 are source-text regex assertions that actively lock in the violating pattern.
findings.expected_state: ART-19 / ARCH-R8 (AGENTS.md:93) and ARCH-004/PAY-007 require the domain write and the event row to commit in the SAME transaction. The SQL path already proves the pattern: the current create_checkout_order inserts the outbox row in-body at 170:550.
assumptions: The ledger-bearing events are precisely the ones written in-transaction by SQL (checkout.completed at 170:568, payment.confirmed, refund.succeeded, order.created at 166:276), so no money is lost or mis-stated by this defect. The at-risk events are notification/webhook/analytics/search tier.

'Silently swallows loss' is the minority path: only a PostgREST schema-cache miss returns null (:7-9,:80-82); all other errors throw, and at checkout-payment-routes.ts:441-443 the throw produces a 500 AFTER the order committed — loud, not silent.

packages/event-core/src/index.ts:1120-1166 writeWithOutbox is NOT a same-transaction helper and is not a valid remedy: it performs the same two-step non-atomic write over a PostgREST-shaped interface with no BEGIN/COMMIT, differing only in that it throws.
This is an ARB-accepted tracked transitional item, sequenced in the architecture decision record.
findings.risk: A gateway isolate that dies, a network blip or a Supabase 5xx between the committed mutation and the outbox POST loses the event permanently with no compensating record: no order-confirmation email, no analytics row, no search projection, no merchant webhook. A mis-migrated or stale-schema-cache environment loses EVERY event from these call sites while the API keeps returning 200.
findings.recommendation: Move each emitDomainEvent call site into the RPC that performs the corresponding domain write, following the migration 166/170 pattern, or introduce a single emit_domain_event RPC called inside the same transaction. Remove the isMissingOptionalEventTable swallow so a failed outbox write fails the request loudly. Unify the checkout.completed idempotency key on the SQL form. Add a validator banning .from('outbox_events') outside the RPC layer.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting a same-transaction emitter for the 38 sites. Confirm with a behavioural test that kills the process between the RPC commit and the outbox write and asserts the event is present.

findings.title: The signed queue tenant envelope expires after 15 minutes, permanently destroying messages once any backlog forms
findings.current_state: verifiedTenantSiteId rejects any tenant-scoped message whose envelope issuedAt is more than 15 minutes from now and throws QueueProcessingError with deterministic:true (services/queue-workers/src/index.ts:172-175). A deterministic error is NOT retried — normalizeDeliveries converts it to quarantinedDelivery (:434-441), which is recorded as dead-lettered and then acked with the rest of the batch at :606. The producer side fails open by contrast: signQueueTenantEnvelope returns the body unsigned when no secret is configured (services/api-gateway/src/lib/queue-tenant-envelope.ts:38-40) while the consumer hard-fails on a missing envelope (:163-166). The notifications queue alone allows 6 retries at 60s (services/queue-workers/wrangler.toml:292-299).
findings.expected_state: A queue message's authenticity window must exceed the queue's own worst-case retry and backlog residence time. A stale envelope means the system is slow, not that the message is malicious.
findings.risk: The moment any queue backs up past 15 minutes, every tenant-scoped message in that backlog is quarantined as expired, recorded dead-lettered, and acked — silent permanent loss of order-confirmation emails at exactly the moment of peak load. The failure mode is self-reinforcing: the busier the platform, the more messages are destroyed. It couples correctness to load.
findings.recommendation: Do not treat envelope expiry as deterministic. Either widen the window beyond worst-case queue residence, re-sign on enqueue-retry, or move authenticity to a non-time-bound HMAC over (siteId, messageId, idempotencyKey) with separate replay protection. Also make the producer fail closed when the secret is absent, matching the consumer.
findings.trigger: Queue residence time exceeding 15 minutes on any queue.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting a re-sign or retry path. Confirm with a behavioural test that delays a message past the window and asserts it is not destroyed.

findings.title: Dead-letter redrive for Cloudflare queues is a no-op — nothing consumes distributed_queue_messages
findings.current_state: POST /runtime/queues/:queueName/redrive-dead-letters (services/api-gateway/src/routes/operations.ts:600-619) calls redrive_distributed_dead_letters, which only flips distributed_queue_messages rows from 'dead-lettered' to 'retrying' and sets available_at = NOW() (000_baseline.sql:6937-6961). Nothing reads them back: claim_distributed_queue_messages, complete_distributed_queue_message, heartbeat_distributed_queue_message and dead_letter_distributed_queue_message all exist in the schema with zero TypeScript callers. The table is written only by persistQueueBatch (services/queue-workers/src/index.ts:249-253) and never claimed. queue-workers declares no [[queues.producers]], so it cannot re-enqueue to Cloudflare either.
findings.expected_state: A dead-letter queue must have a drain path that actually re-delivers messages, or its existence must be documented as audit-only. An operator action labelled 'redrive' must redrive.
assumptions: The OUTBOX dead-letter path is different and does work: replay_outbox_dead_letter (000_baseline.sql:7220-7261) resets outbox_events rows that the relay then re-claims.
findings.risk: During an incident an operator calls redrive, receives { redriven_count: N }, and reasonably concludes the messages are being reprocessed. Nothing happens. The dead-lettered work — order-confirmation emails, analytics events, search projections — is permanently lost while the operator believes it has been recovered. This removes the only recovery lever after a mass dead-letter event.
findings.recommendation: Either implement a consumer that claims distributed_queue_messages with status 'retrying' and re-executes the delivery (the four supporting RPCs already exist), or add a [[queues.producers]] binding to queue-workers and re-enqueue to the source Cloudflare queue. Until one lands, make the endpoint return an explicit not-implemented error rather than a success count.
findings.trigger: Unconditional; the endpoint is actively misleading during incidents.
findings.verification: Falsify by finding a consumer of distributed_queue_messages. Confirm by dead-lettering a message, calling redrive, and asserting it is or is not reprocessed.

findings.title: auth_password_set_intents carries a live PUBLIC USING(true) WITH CHECK(true) policy — a schema-level account-takeover primitive
findings.current_state: database/supabase/migrations/078_password_set_intents.sql enables RLS on the table (:41) and then creates CREATE POLICY "Service role manages auth password set intents" ... USING (true) WITH CHECK (true) with NO TO clause (:50-55, inside a DO/IF NOT EXISTS block). In PostgreSQL a policy without TO applies to PUBLIC, so this PERMISSIVE policy passes for every role including anon. No later migration drops or replaces it (checked across 073-197). No REVOKE exists for this table — migration 163's REVOKE list at :202-215 covers 11 other tables only. The table's own header (078:1-3) states it is the authority binding identity password creation to a freshly verified OTP.
findings.expected_state: Constitution R-3 / SEC-R6: no public USING(true); identity and tenant tables fail closed with an explicit TO clause and a real predicate. Migration 163's own header (:1-4) documents this exact defect class as a P2 emergency and names the cause: policies without an explicit TO clause apply to PUBLIC.
assumptions: Exploitability additionally requires anon/authenticated to hold the table INSERT grant. Supabase provisions that by default and no migration revokes it for this table, but the live grant set is UNKNOWN without database access.
Applied state in production is UNKNOWN: a migration file is not proof that it ran.

Adversarially corrected S0->S1, VERIFIED-SOURCE->INFERRED. The policy and the consume path are VERIFIED-SOURCE; the decisive precondition (whether anon/authenticated holds the table GRANT) is UNKNOWN because 000_baseline.sql is a --no-privileges pg_dump with zero GRANT statements across 28,083 lines.

Scope narrowed: the FK at 078:7 targets public.users_custom (merchant/platform identities) ONLY. Storefront customers use store_customers/customer_credentials and the separate migration-077 flow, and are NOT reachable via this table.
No deployed LetBuyy surface publishes the anon key (no NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_* in app source; no browser-side Supabase client). It must be obtained, not merely read from the product.
findings.risk: An unauthenticated caller holding only the public Supabase anon key can INSERT a password-set intent row for an arbitrary user_id/email and then drive the identity-platform password-set flow to take over any merchant or customer account.
findings.recommendation: Ship a migration that drops the policy and recreates it FOR ALL TO service_role USING (true) WITH CHECK (true), plus REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.auth_password_set_intents FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, with a paired rollback. Verify live grants first with information_schema.role_table_grants.
findings.verification: Run \dp public.auth_password_set_intents against the live database. If anon/authenticated holds INSERT, this is S0. See 04_LIVE_DEPLOYMENT_TRUTH.md L-10.

findings.title: Nineteen PUBLIC-effective policies survive replay-final; 13 are genuine defects and 6 are deliberate allowlisted catalogs

Beyond the ~90 correctly scoped TO service_role, these remain PUBLIC-effective: collection_products (000_baseline:26645), collections (:26652), gift_cards (:26666), onboarding_attempts (:26694), pages (:26708), store_surveys (:26743), ai_usage (:23960), plans (:24277), employee_roles (:24284), audit_logs (:24380), contact_submissions (:25808), leads (:25815), analytics_events (:25822), app_collections / app_collection_items / app_featured_placements / app_discovery_events (100:133,145,152,155), employee_permissions (107:121, FOR SELECT USING(true)); plus explicit anon/authenticated true policies on skill_endorsements (:24270, :25865) and smart_collections (:25924). findings.title: Internal service-to-service authentication fails OPEN by default on a secret shared across ten-plus runtimes
findings.current_state: isLegacyAcceptEnabled(env) returns true unless INTERNAL_AUTH_LEGACY_ACCEPT is explicitly set to false/0/off/no/disabled; the code comment states 'Default ON — unset or empty means legacy single-secret acceptance is active' (services/api-gateway/src/lib/internal-auth.ts:41-47). findings.title: Security-critical validators certify behaviour by grepping for identifier names
findings.current_state: session-security-validator.mjs is entirely readFile(...).includes(fragment): it certifies internal secret isolation, replay JTI, session rotation, MFA and perimeter by asserting strings like 'consumedInternalJtis', "status: 'replayed'" and 'INTERNAL_API_SECRET_PREVIOUS' appear in source. stepup-crypto-validator.mjs certifies HMAC step-up by asserting security-controls.ts contains the literal 'HMAC'. canonical-ledger-only-validator.mjs checks canonical-ledger evidence at FILE scope, not call-site scope, so any file that mentions ledger_entries anywhere may perform an arbitrary .from('payments').insert(). identity-sole-issuer-validator.mjs detects only `new SignJWT`, `jwt.sign(` and HS256 protected headers, so signing via crypto.subtle or a helper is invisible to it — which is exactly how ARCH-RESEARCH-016 passes the gate.

Move sole-issuer and step-up to behavioural tests modelled on services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/identity-issuer-d3.test.ts:93-153, which is the one identity test in the repository that generates keys and exercises real crypto.

findings.title: Approximately 38 percent of the 582 test files are source-greps that never load the code under test
findings.current_state: Scanning tests/, services/, packages/ and apps/ (excluding node_modules and worktrees): 582 test files; 243 use readFileSync with no import of a relative or @letbuyy module; subtracting the ~20 tests/executable suites that legitimately read migration SQL and then execute it via docker leaves ~223 (38%) that are pure source-greps. A further 142 mix source-grep with real imports. Concentrations: services/api-gateway/src/__tests__ (46), tests/contracts (43), tests/launch (38), tests/federation (16), tests/theme-engine (10), tests/performance (10). Independently, 221 of 239 files under tests/ and 68 of 82 under services/api-gateway/src/__tests__ call readFileSync against source and assert on its text.
findings.expected_state: Test-count coverage claims should distinguish tests that execute code from tests that pattern-match its text. ART-17 requires a real parity/security/performance harness; TEST-R1 requires nine test classes per winner.
evidence: node walk over tests/ services/ packages/ apps/: total=582, readFileSync-without-import=243, mixed=142, imports-only=180, other=17
assumptions: A genuinely behavioural tier does exist and runs on every PR — see ARCH-RESEARCH-110. The risk is that it is invisible when averaged into the 582-file count.
findings.risk: The headline test count implies behavioural assurance it does not carry. A source-grep test locks in the current text of a file, so it resists refactoring while permitting behavioural regressions. Conclusions drawn from these suites ('parity green', 'contract green') are structurally unsound.
findings.recommendation: Label the source-grep suites explicitly as structural contracts or lints — rename the directory or the runner — so they cannot be cited as behavioural evidence, and report two numbers (executing tests / structural contracts) wherever coverage is claimed.
findings.verification: Falsify by re-running the walk with a different classifier. Confirm by publishing the two-number split in AGENTS.md.

findings.title: No load or performance testing exists anywhere in the repository
findings.current_state: All 10 files under tests/performance/ are readFileSync + assert.ok(source.includes(...)) over gateway route source and wrangler.toml; none executes a request, a query or a timer. No k6, artillery, autocannon or wrk dependency exists anywhere. The only timing artifact is packages/theme-engine/test/liquid-render-benchmark.test.ts, which renders a fixture N=25 times in one Node process at concurrency 1 against an in-memory bundle with no HTTP, no database and no concurrent client.
findings.expected_state: A platform declaring a 100 -> 1,000 -> 10,000 merchant scale envelope needs at least one test that applies concurrent load to a real endpoint.
assumptions: Two genuine contention proofs exist in tests/executable/ (inventory oversell under Promise.allSettled, 12-writer ledger idempotency). Both are single-container and prove correctness under contention, not throughput.
findings.risk: There is no evidence at any commit about throughput, p95 latency under concurrency, connection-pool behaviour, queue drain rate, or the merchant count at which anything degrades. The scale envelope is unsubstantiated by testing, and every capacity figure in this packet is derived from static reading plus vendor documentation rather than measurement.
findings.recommendation: Build the programme described in 13_TEST_AND_LOAD_VALIDATION.md. The minimum useful first test is a concurrent storefront read test that measures cache hit ratio and origin RPS, because it falsifies or confirms ARCH-RESEARCH-005 directly.
findings.trigger: Before any claim that a band is served.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting an executing load test. Confirm by publishing a measured p95 and throughput curve.

findings.title: No timeout on any external provider call except the storefront edge proxy
findings.current_state: Every outbound call site in the deployed runtimes uses bare fetch or an SDK call with no AbortSignal, no deadline and no retry: Razorpay (packages/infrastructure/razorpay-adapter/index.ts:100,187,199), Twilio WhatsApp (whatsapp-commerce-adapter/index.ts:244), Turnstile siteverify (api-gateway middleware/security.ts:237 and identity-platform lib/turnstile.ts:85), Upstash Redis (rateLimit.ts:204,694), Supabase REST (supabase-adapter/index.ts:79,98,118,138), Supabase RPC from the webhook worker (webhook-service/src/index.ts:188), Resend via SDK (resend-adapter/index.ts:66). The only request-path timeout in the repository is apps/storefront-runtime/src/proxy.ts:110,121,161 (AbortSignal.timeout(3000)).
findings.expected_state: Every cross-network call on a request path carries a deadline; Cloudflare Workers provide AbortSignal.timeout at no cost.
findings.risk: A slow (not failed) provider converts into held Worker invocations and held database connections across the whole fleet. Because the query-cost limiter itself performs a KV or Redis round trip before admitting a request, a slow rate-limit backend stalls every /v1 route simultaneously. Partial provider degradation is precisely the failure mode this leaves undefended, and 07_CAPACITY_MODEL.md Finding C-4 shows latency converts directly into pooler exhaustion.
findings.recommendation: Add AbortSignal.timeout to every call site with per-provider budgets (Turnstile ~2s, Razorpay ~5s, Redis ~500ms, Supabase REST ~5s), or adopt the already-written provider-resilience-adapter (ARCH-RESEARCH-009). Add a validator that fails when a new outbound fetch is added without a signal.
findings.trigger: Unconditional resilience fix; escalates on any provider p99 above its budget.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting a deadline on any of the listed call sites. Confirm with a fault-injection test that stalls one provider and measures gateway concurrency consumption.

findings.title: provider-resilience-adapter — the repository's entire timeout/retry/circuit-breaker/fallback implementation — has zero call sites
findings.current_state: packages/infrastructure/provider-resilience-adapter/index.ts implements executeProviderCall (:193-255), withProviderTimeout (:257-269), providerBackoffMs (:84-86), classifyProviderHealth (:88-109), decideProviderFallback (:111-118), planProviderRecovery (:120-160) and ProviderResilienceOperationsRuntime (:162-191). A repo-wide search for those symbols and for the '@letbuyy/infrastructure/provider-resilience-adapter' subpath outside the package itself and its export map returns nothing.
findings.expected_state: Either the adapter wraps the money and notification provider calls, or it is not presented as platform resilience.
findings.risk: An architecture review reading the package list concludes the platform has provider resilience. It has the types and the algorithms and applies none of them. Defined-but-never-called is the most misleading category of readiness evidence.
findings.recommendation: Wire executeProviderCall around the Razorpay, Resend, Twilio and Turnstile call sites with per-provider policies, and add a validator that fails if a new outbound provider fetch is added outside the adapter. Closing this closes ARCH-RESEARCH-008 at the same time.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting one production import of the adapter. Confirm by counting call sites after the change.

findings.title: No saturation-driven load shedding, backpressure, degraded mode, or read-only mode exists
findings.current_state: What exists: per-key fixed-window and cost-weighted rate limiting returning 429 with Retry-After (rateLimit.ts:479,1005,1091,1171) and 503 when the backend is down (:466-479,:990-994); the app-platform kill switch; a per-flag kill_switch type in shared-types; a queue drain budget and per-isolate circuit breaker (platform-queue-consumer.ts:233,252-262,309-331); a KV backoff breaker (rateLimit.ts:613). What does not exist: any admission decision keyed to queue depth, database connection count, database latency or Worker CPU; any read-only or maintenance mode; any feature degradation under load. /v1/health/queues returns 503 only for a missing binding (index.ts:332-348), never for backlog. The gateway does count backlog rows (index.ts:435-454) but reduces the result to a boolean hasWork.
findings.expected_state: Under saturation the platform should preferentially shed non-critical reads (analytics, export, search) and keep checkout and payment serving.
findings.risk: Rate limiting is per-key fairness, not global protection. A legitimate aggregate load spike across many merchants passes every limiter and saturates the shared PostgreSQL, at which point everything including checkout fails together rather than degrading. There is no lever to turn off analytics, exports or search and preserve the money path.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a cheap global pressure signal (the existing backlog counts at index.ts:435-454 plus the PostgreSQL connection probe of ARCH-RESEARCH-021) and use it to shed the routes calculateQueryCost already labels expensive.
findings.trigger: Wire the signal first; shed when pooled connection utilisation exceeds 70% or outbox backlog age exceeds 15 minutes.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting any admission decision keyed to a saturation signal. Confirm with a load test that drives the database to saturation and observes whether checkout survives.

findings.title: Host-to-site resolution is uncached and is a synchronous fail-closed dependency on 100% of storefront requests
findings.current_state: resolveAccess fetches ${gateway}/v1/internal/store-access/resolve?host= with cache:'no-store' and AbortSignal.timeout(3000) on every request (apps/storefront-runtime/src/proxy.ts:112-142, invoked at :346). The gateway handler runs resolveStorefrontSiteByHost, which issues a sites SELECT by subdomain, or for custom domains a sites SELECT plus a site_domains SELECT plus a second sites SELECT (services/api-gateway/src/middleware/store-context.ts:209-254). No KV, Cache API or in-process memo wraps it. validGateCookie (proxy.ts:245-256) documents the no-store requirement so an access-mode change is honoured immediately.
findings.expected_state: A per-request tenant resolution on the hottest path should be served from a short-TTL versioned cache — the same KV/Cache-API mechanism already built for storefront JSON — with explicit invalidation on access-mode and domain mutation.
findings.risk: One gateway round-trip plus 1-3 PostgreSQL queries on 100% of storefront traffic that no cache layer absorbs; a custom-domain host costs 3 queries before any content is fetched. It is also a total-outage single point of failure: any gateway error, timeout or missing INTERNAL_API_SECRET turns every storefront on the platform into a 503 holding page (proxy.ts:347-354).
findings.recommendation: Cache the resolve response in KV or the Cache API keyed by host with a 5-30s TTL plus an explicit purge on access-mode, publish-status and domain mutations; keep the fail-closed path for a genuine miss. Add negative caching for unknown hosts so an unknown-host flood cannot amplify into database load (see ARCH-RESEARCH-086).
findings.trigger: Already binding at every band; measure as gateway invocations per storefront page view.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting a cache in front of resolveAccess. Confirm by counting /v1/internal/store-access/resolve invocations against storefront page views.

findings.title: Cache tags are declared but revalidateTag is never called, and only theme publish bumps the storefront cache version
findings.current_state: Storefront reads attach tags such as storefront:<subdomain>, :products and :product:<id> across 19 call sites (store-service.ts:110,431-432,473-474; product-service.ts:29-31,44,57,72-75; review-service.ts:24-26; content-service.ts:84; composition-engine.tsx:387,463). A repo-wide search for revalidateTag returns zero hits in apps/storefront-runtime, services/* and packages/*. Separately, bumpStorefrontCacheVersion / purgeStorefrontCache have exactly one call site: purgeThemeStorefrontCache in routes/themes.ts:140-158, called on publish (:642) and rollback (:697). Products, collections, categories, navigation, pages, policies and blog routes call neither. The per-key purge targets literal version '0', so once any bump has occurred it deletes a key that no longer exists, and cache.delete is colo-local on Cloudflare so only the version bump actually works.
findings.expected_state: Tag-based invalidation is the only reason to pay the cost of tagging; every mutation that changes a cached storefront projection should bump the tenant's cache version so the Cache API keys rotate.
evidence: rg -n revalidateTag -> 0 hits outside next/cache imports in unrelated admin apps
assumptions: The staleness is currently masked because the Data Cache never hits at all (ARCH-RESEARCH-005). Fixing the cache key without adding invalidation will surface up-to-60s staleness immediately.
findings.risk: A merchant who edits a price, hides a product or changes the menu sees the storefront lag by up to the TTL with no way to force propagation, and the tag metadata creates a false impression that targeted invalidation exists. Correct invalidation is the precondition for raising the TTL, which is the cheapest way to raise the cacheable fraction at 10,000 merchants.
findings.recommendation: Call bumpStorefrontCacheVersion from every storefront-visible mutation (products, collections, navigation, CMS pages, policies, blog, custom domain), drop the misleading version-'0' purge, and either wire a gateway-to-storefront revalidate webhook that calls revalidateTag or delete the tags and document TTL-only semantics.
findings.trigger: Fix jointly with ARCH-RESEARCH-005 before raising any TTL.
findings.verification: Falsify by finding a revalidateTag call or a second bump site. Confirm by editing a product and measuring propagation delay.

findings.title: Non-200 storefront responses are never cached, so 404 and scrape traffic reaches PostgreSQL unthrottled
findings.current_state: cachedJson writes to the Cache API only when the produced status is exactly 200 (services/api-gateway/src/lib/storefront-cache.ts:126-128), and jsonResponse sets Cache-Control: no-store for every non-200 (:42). The product-detail producer runs loadPublishedStore plus a products SELECT before returning 404 (public-routes.ts:834-852). The uncached /:subdomain/status route and resolveAccess (ARCH-RESEARCH-011) also execute a sites SELECT for a nonexistent handle.
findings.expected_state: Negative results for a public, enumerable key space (product slugs, page slugs, unknown subdomains) should be short-TTL cached so an enumeration burst cannot be amplified into database load.
findings.risk: An unauthenticated crawler iterating /product/<random> on one store drives 2-3 uncached PostgreSQL queries per request indefinitely. Combined with the uncached resolveAccess and /status calls, an unknown-host flood is a cheap way to saturate the shared pooled connections.
findings.recommendation: Cache 404 bodies with a short TTL (5-15s) under the same versioned key, and add negative caching for unknown hosts in the store-access resolver.
findings.trigger: 404 rate above a stated share of storefront requests.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting non-200 caching. Confirm by driving an enumeration burst and counting database queries.

findings.title: Cache hit ratio has no emission point anywhere — it exists only as a response header, and the storefront render log hard-codes cache_hit: null
findings.current_state: cachedJson classifies every storefront read as HIT, MISS or BYPASS and sets it on X-Storefront-Cache (services/api-gateway/src/lib/storefront-cache.ts:36-56, :113-128), but emits no metric. The observability middleware's Analytics Engine blobs are path, method, statusClass, authSource, errorCode, CF-IPCountry and CF-Ray (observability.ts:175-183) and the PostgreSQL dimensions are route, method, status_code, status_class, latency_ms, error counters, auth_source, country and colo (:278-290) — neither carries cache state. The Cache API uses an internal synthetic key host (letbuyy-storefront-cache.internal), so Cloudflare zone-level cache analytics do not cover it either. The storefront canary render log writes cache_hit: null with the comment 'field present; NOT CONNECTED until per-request render cache is wired' (composition-engine.tsx:672).
findings.expected_state: Cache hit ratio is the primary capacity lever for a storefront and must be measurable per namespace and per tenant before any scale decision.
findings.risk: There is no way to detect from production telemetry that tier 1 is at 0% hit rate (ARCH-RESEARCH-005), or to observe the stampede after a theme publish, or to notice a cache-effectiveness regression. Storefront read load against PostgreSQL is hit-ratio dependent and read-path capacity headroom cannot be estimated without it. Capacity planning for 1,000 to 10,000 merchants would be done blind.
findings.recommendation: Append the existing X-Storefront-Cache classification as a blob and a 0/1 double to the Analytics Engine data point already written per request, keyed by cache namespace and site id. This is a one-line-per-site change on an existing emission path and it is the measurement that falsifies or confirms ARCH-RESEARCH-005.
findings.trigger: Unconditional; precondition for the cache work.
findings.verification: Falsify by finding an emission point. Confirm by querying hit ratio per namespace from the emitted dataset.

findings.title: Random X-Request-ID on every server-side gateway fetch defeats the Next Data Cache and per-request memoisation
findings.current_state: apps/storefront-runtime/src/lib/api/client.ts:45 sets a fresh X-Request-ID: crypto.randomUUID() on every server-side gateway fetch. In the installed Next 16.1.6, both the Data Cache key (node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/incremental-cache/index.js:240-259, materialising headers at :240 and stripping only traceparent/tracestate at :242-243) and the request-memoisation key (dist/server/lib/dedupe-fetch.js:60-82, installed at patch-fetch.js:928) include the request headers. Every one of the 19 storefrontReadInit(30-60s, tags) reads therefore writes a Data Cache entry under a key that can never be read again, and duplicate fetches within one render are not deduplicated. No React.cache() or unstable_cache() wrapper exists in apps/storefront-runtime/src to compensate, and the route is fully dynamic so no Full Route Cache absorbs the duplicates. A product-detail render issues roughly 22 gateway fetches where ~8 distinct URLs exist.
findings.expected_state: The code's own intent: storefrontReadInit sets next: { revalidate, tags } precisely so these reads are cached. The fix is free — services/api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts:292 already synthesizes a request ID when the header is absent, so removing the client-side random header costs no traceability.
assumptions: The governance framing is corrected: LETBUYY_CONSTITUTION.md:260 governs a 3-tier KV-versioned Worker cache, not the Next Data Cache, and apps/storefront-runtime uses no KV. No constitutional invariant is breached; the defect rests on the code's own intent.
Impact is cost and latency only, with graceful degradation — no correctness, tenancy, money or security consequence.
Necessary but not sufficient: revalidateTag is never called (ARCH-RESEARCH-084), so even with the key fixed tier 1 would serve an unpurgeable 30-60s stale window.
findings.risk: Roughly 2.5-3x amplification of gateway invocations and downstream PostgreSQL reads on every storefront page render.
findings.recommendation: Delete the client-side X-Request-ID header. This is the single cheapest item in the packet and is component (a) of ARCH-RESEARCH-005.
findings.verification: Falsify by measuring a non-zero Data Cache hit rate today. Confirm by counting distinct gateway invocations per product-detail render before and after.

findings.title: No /store/* route can populate the Next Full Route Cache: a cookie read in the tenant layout forces the entire subtree to dynamic rendering
findings.current_state: apps/storefront-runtime/src/app/store/[subdomain]/layout.tsx:76 unconditionally awaits resolveThemePreviewToken(subdomain) with no explicit token, so apps/storefront-runtime/src/lib/theme-preview-server.ts:12 `await cookies()` always executes. The layout wraps every route under /store/[subdomain]/**, so the whole subtree bails to dynamic rendering and every `export const revalidate` in it (layout.tsx:20; product/[productId]/page.tsx:12; collections/[slug]/page.tsx:12; page.tsx:10; shop:11; products:11; blog:20; [...path]:9) cannot produce a Full Route Cache entry. The escape hatch is genuinely absent: next.config.ts has no experimental block and Next 16.1.6 defaults cacheComponents:false (node_modules/next/dist/server/config-shared.js:101). Note src/proxy.ts IS the middleware — Next 16 renamed middleware.ts to proxy.ts.
findings.expected_state: The governed model is SSR/ISR plus Worker cache; today it delivers SSR plus Worker cache, not ISR.
assumptions: 'No edge HTML cache exists' is NOT established. next.config.ts:124-126 sets Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600 on source '/:path*', and Next 16 preserves user-set Cache-Control (send-payload.js:58-62 skips its own header when one is already present). Whether Vercel's edge stores a function response carrying `public, max-age=300` with no s-maxage is provider behaviour with no authorized test here. The correct statement is: no Next full-route/ISR cache, plus a shared-cache HTTP directive configured whose honouring is unverified.

An API-tier edge cache does exist (services/api-gateway/src/lib/storefront-cache.ts using caches.default with KV versioning, STOREFRONT_CACHE='on' in all three envs), so bursts do not reach PostgreSQL 1:1 — the 1:1 consequence comes from ARCH-RESEARCH-090, not from this.
findings.risk: Every storefront request costs a full SSR render plus the downstream fetch fan-out; nothing is servable from the CDN. This sets the absolute ceiling on storefront throughput and removes the buffer in front of Vercel's burst governor (ARCH-RESEARCH-051).
findings.recommendation: Move the theme-preview cookie read behind a Suspense boundary or into a dedicated preview route so the public storefront tree can prerender, then re-verify with `next build` output that /store/[subdomain]/product/[productId] reports as static or ISR. This is component (b) of ARCH-RESEARCH-005.
findings.verification: Falsify with a `next build` output showing any /store/* route as static or ISR. Confirm by reading the build output today.

findings.title: Public storefront order create performs ~15 database round-trips and holds a per-SKU product row lock for a 30-40 statement transaction
findings.current_state: Measured from source for a one-line cart: loadPublishedStore 1; createPublicStorefrontTenantContext 4 (site_roles, site_role_permissions, subscriptions, resolve_site_entitlements — lib/tenant-context.ts:115/131/76 and execution/saas-execution.adapter.ts:66); idempotency.begin 1; resolveShippingRate 1-2; tax_registrations 1; tax_rates 1; a products price lookup per line item inside a loop (checkout-payment-routes.ts:338); assertOrderQuota 2; create_checkout_order 1; outbox upsert 1; idempotency.complete 1. Inside the single RPC transaction: SELECT FROM products FOR UPDATE per SKU (166:87) and SELECT FROM inventory_levels FOR UPDATE (141:121), both held to COMMIT alongside coupon evaluation, gift-card ledger writes, GST computation, five INSERT blocks, the outbox insert and its shadow-mirror trigger. Shared coupon codes add a second global serialization point: UPDATE promotion_codes SET usage_count = usage_count + 1 and UPDATE coupons SET usage_count (170:419-427).
findings.expected_state: A checkout write should hold its narrowest lock for the shortest possible window and should not re-read data the RPC will read again.
assumptions: Steady state at the governed envelope is roughly 0.7 orders/second platform-wide, so aggregate throughput is not the binding constraint. Indian commerce is spiky: a 100x flash-sale peak against a single-SKU row lock held for a 30-40 statement transaction is where this design fails first.
findings.risk: On a hot SKU all concurrent buyers serialize on the products row for the full transaction — a much wider lock than the inventory row that actually needs protecting. Lock hold time, not request rate, is what exhausts the pooler (ARCH-RESEARCH-053).
findings.recommendation: Downgrade the products FOR UPDATE to a plain read (price is immutable within the transaction and inventory is already locked separately); batch the per-item price lookup into one .in('id', ids) query or have the RPC return the GST breakdown; cache the anonymous storefront tenant context. Solve hot-SKU contention with optimistic version columns or sharded counters — never session-level advisory locks, which neither Supavisor nor Hyperdrive support.
findings.trigger: Any single SKU exceeding a stated concurrent-checkout rate, or mean transaction duration above 100 ms.
findings.verification: Falsify by re-tracing the round trips. Confirm with pg_locks sampling during a concurrent single-SKU checkout test.

findings.title: Every order creation runs an unindexed exact COUNT over the store's lifetime orders for the monthly quota check
findings.current_state: assertOrderQuota runs before every create_checkout_order (execution/order-execution.adapter.ts:154) and, when the plan has a finite orders_monthly limit (free 50, starter 250, growth 2500 — packages/billing-core/src/index.ts:702/740/778), issues .from('orders').select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true }).eq('store_id', ...).gte('created_at', periodStart).is('deleted_at', null) (:385-390). It is preceded by a resolve_site_entitlements RPC (:375). Available indexes on orders are idx_orders_active (store_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, idx_orders_store (store_id), idx_orders_status and idx_orders_site_id — there is no (store_id, created_at) composite.
findings.expected_state: A per-request quota gate on the hottest write path should be O(1) against a counter or a covering index, not an exact count.
findings.risk: count exact forces a full index scan of every non-deleted order for the store, then a heap filter on created_at. Cost grows linearly with a merchant's lifetime order count and is paid on EVERY checkout, so the highest-volume and most valuable stores degrade first. It also adds two round-trips to the synchronous order path.
findings.recommendation: Add CREATE INDEX orders_store_created_at_idx ON public.orders (store_id, created_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, and better, read the monthly counter from the existing usage-metering table (record_site_usage already meters 'orders' at order-execution.adapter.ts:201) instead of counting orders. This is the cheapest latency win on the checkout path.
findings.verification: Falsify by finding the composite index. Confirm with EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the count query for a high-volume store.

findings.title: The storefront layout fetches up to 100 full product rows on every page render purely to seed header search, and the bootstrap payload is duplicated and fetched three times per render
findings.current_state: apps/storefront-runtime/src/app/store/[subdomain]/layout.tsx:99-112 calls ProductService.getProductsByStoreSubdomain (limit 100) on every route under /store/[subdomain], commented 'Fetch products for search'. The gateway returns PRODUCT_SELECT_FULL including description, images, tags, variants and seo_description (routes/storefront.ts:353-354) and, with PRODUCT_VARIANTS_RELATIONAL_READS='on', hydrates product_variants for all 100 in a second query (:493-530). Separately, mapPublicStorePayload emits both release_config and template_snapshot as the identical object (packages/tenant-core/src/index.ts:503-521) while the storefront reads only one (store-service.ts:548), and because request dedupe is defeated (ARCH-RESEARCH-005) GET /storefront/:subdomain is fetched three times per product-detail render.

findings.risk: Every storefront page — including cart, account and checkout — pays a 100-row full-column product fetch plus a variant join, and the theme bundle (24 Liquid sections for the urban-kicks theme) is transferred six times per page render (two copies across three fetches). Together these are the largest gateway-egress and RSC-payload contributors, and they scale with catalogue width rather than with what the page renders.

findings.trigger: Unconditional efficiency fix; pairs with ARCH-RESEARCH-005.

findings.title: bcryptjs cost 12 runs inside the api-gateway Worker on the login path with no declared CPU limit
findings.current_state: MERCHANT_PASSWORD_BCRYPT_ROUNDS = 12 using the pure-JavaScript bcryptjs package (lib/merchant-password.ts:1-12), invoked synchronously on the login hot path at routes/auth.ts:527 and on hashing at :499. Customer registration also runs bcryptjs (storefront/customer-registration.ts:6). services/api-gateway/wrangler.toml declares no [limits] block, so the account-default CPU ceiling applies.
findings.expected_state: Cost 12 is correct for security; running it in pure JS inside a CPU-metered edge isolate is a deployment-shape decision that needs an explicit CPU budget and a measured p99.
assumptions: No CPU-time measurement exists in the repository; the throughput claim is INFERRED from the algorithm's iteration count.
findings.risk: bcryptjs is materially slower than a native implementation and cost 12 is 4,096 iterations. Under a login storm this becomes the CPU bottleneck of the whole gateway, and if the per-invocation CPU ceiling is exceeded the Worker is terminated mid-login, producing failures that look like an outage rather than a rate limit. Because Workers CPU time is billed, credential stuffing converts directly into cost even when every attempt fails.
findings.recommendation: Measure actual CPU ms per bcrypt.compare on staging via wrangler tail, then declare an explicit [limits] cpu_ms in wrangler.toml so the failure mode is a clean error rather than an unbounded bill. Evaluate moving password verification behind a PostgreSQL SECURITY DEFINER function using pgcrypto.
findings.trigger: Login rate above a stated threshold, or measured CPU ms approaching the declared ceiling.
findings.verification: Falsify by exhibiting a [limits] block. Confirm by measuring CPU ms per login invocation.
